content.content:
Every invocation that writes graph state runs in the trunk working copy.

Part of this is already fixed, and this node takes it as given. Only creation, recording and removal are the invocations that bracket, and those invocations run in the trunk (uqqswnsy). The marker stack they write is one file in the working copy whose root holds the store root, read and written only there and never from a draft workspace (uqqswnsy), and the CLI is required to read and write it only from the trunk working copy and neither read nor write it from a draft (zmvxksws). None of that is restated here as this node's own rule, narrowed to a smaller set, or decided a second time: the bracketing set stays exactly creation, recording and removal, a recording still draws one bracket on the trunk's marker file, and the marker stack keeps its one fixed place. The confinement below is not a fourth bracketing invocation: it draws no bracket, and being confined to the trunk does not make any invocation bracket.

What those clauses do not fix is the rest of the invocations that write graph state. Undo and redo write graph state — they revert and reapply earlier graph writes — and they are not among the invocations that bracket, because only creation, recording and removal bracket (uqqswnsy). Any other verb that writes graph state without bracketing is in the same position. Nothing in the bracketing clauses reaches them, and the store's root does not supply the missing rule: the store is opened on the trunk root from any working copy (lotlstzr), so an undo or redo admitted in a draft would write through a trunk-rooted store into the trunk's graph while its caller stood in a draft. The trunk-run of the bracketing set is therefore a rule about that subset, not yet a rule about graph writes.

This node adds that rule, as its own. Every invocation that writes graph state runs in the trunk working copy: creation, recording and removal as already fixed (uqqswnsy), and equally undo, redo, and any other verb that writes graph state. The confinement follows from the write, not from the bracket.

An invocation that writes graph state and runs in a working copy other than the trunk refuses. It refuses because of the working copy it ran in, not because the trunk could not be found: the trunk is still resolved from the invocation workspace, and a draft workspace is a working copy of the same tree whose repository entry names the trunk, so resolution succeeds and the refusal is a decision about admission, not a failure of resolution (lotlstzr). The refusal names the workspace the invocation ran in — the working copy whose root the caller stood in — so the caller can tell which workspace was refused. It writes nothing: no node document or edge, no marker, no journal entry, no exclude entry, no blob, no draft record, and no change. It reads no marker either, so the requirement that the CLI read and write the marker stack only from the trunk working copy (zmvxksws) holds in both directions: where the stack is handled it is handled in the trunk (uqqswnsy), and where the invocation is refused no part of the stack is read or written at all. It opens nothing on the invocation workspace root, creates no state directory there, probes no other working copy, and takes no second root; the store still holds the one root it holds and lends it, with no reach of its own (ppwnzwwy). Because it writes nothing, it leaves the graph, the marker stack, the journal and the draft registry exactly as they stood.

The trunk is named by place, not by label. The working copy the rule requires is the one whose root holds the store root (uqqswnsy); no change id and no workspace name makes an invocation trunk-side, renaming the trunk does not move the boundary, and checking out a different change there does not either. The rule is applied to the working copy the invocation runs in, not to the change that working copy has checked out.

The jj runner stays on the invocation workspace. The confinement is over admission to graph writes, not over the working copy the runner edits: the runner's anchor remains the root the invocation workspace resolves (lotlstzr), and this node does not move it to the trunk. The two roots remain two answers to two questions — the store's root is the trunk's, the runner's anchor is the invocation's — and the rule changes neither.

`draft` and `drafts` are outside the refused set and keep working from any workspace. Opening a draft writes a registry record that creates no node and no change and records no edit into a node (uqqswnsy); listing drafts writes no graph state at all. Neither invocation writes graph state, so neither is refused outside the trunk. Non-mutating invocations are outside the set for the same reason: the rule is about writes to graph state, not about reads of it, help or version.

Nothing here narrows what a prerequisite fixes. The store is opened on the one trunk root whatever working copy the caller used, and which working copy the invocation runs in does not move the store (lotlstzr); the store holds that root and has no reach of its own (ppwnzwwy); the bracketing invocations run in the trunk and draw their brackets on the trunk's marker file (uqqswnsy); and the CLI reads and writes the marker stack only from the trunk working copy and never from a draft (zmvxksws). In particular, the property that a call made from a draft workspace reaches the same store on the same trunk root as a call made from the trunk (lotlstzr) is about the root the store takes, not about which calls are admitted; this node adds admission and leaves that property's answer — the trunk root, never the invocation root — exactly as it stands. A refusal that writes nothing is not a second root and does not move the store.

Not settled here: the wording, stream and exit status of the refusal; the format in which the workspace is named; how the invocation establishes that its working copy is not the trunk; and the full enumeration of verbs that write graph state. Each can change without moving the rule this node settles: every invocation that writes graph state runs in the trunk working copy, and one that runs elsewhere refuses, names the workspace it ran in, and writes nothing.
content.rationale: uqqswnsy already fixes the bracketing half: only creation, recording and removal bracket, those invocations run in the trunk, and the marker stack is read and written only from that working copy and never from a draft; zmvxksws records the same property for the CLI as a requirement. The node takes both as given and says so, so neither is re-decided and the bracketing set is neither widened nor narrowed. What those clauses leave out is the graph-writing invocation that does not bracket. Undo and redo write graph state and, by uqqswnsy's "only", never bracket; if they were admitted in a draft they would still write through the trunk-rooted store (lotlstzr), so the gap is not cosmetic. The addition is therefore the extension of the trunk-run to the whole graph-writing set, and the refusal that enforces it: refusal by the working copy the invocation ran in, naming that workspace, writing nothing. The refusal is not a root rule — ppwnzwwy gives the store one root and no reach — and it is not lotlstzr's refusal for an unresolvable trunk, because resolution succeeds from a draft and the decision is about admission. `draft` and `drafts` are excluded because their writes are registry writes, not graph writes (uqqswnsy), and non-mutating invocations because the rule is about writes. The jj runner stays where lotlstzr puts it: confinement is over admission, not over the working copy the invocation edits. Left out are the refusal's wording, stream and exit status, the format in which the workspace is named, the detection mechanism, and the full verb enumeration; each is owned elsewhere and none can move the rule.
